def predict(probe):
    # Main idea: reverse the string, then strip trailing whitespace from the
    # reversed string (which corresponds to leading whitespace of the original).
    # Evidence:
    # - "apple" -> "elppa" [E1]
    # - " lead" -> "dael " (reverse "dael ", leading space moves to end) [E2]
    # - "trail " -> "liart" (original trailing space becomes leading in reverse,
    #   then stripped) [E2]
    # - "test case  " -> "esac tset" (trailing spaces stripped) [E3]
    # - "  x  " -> "x  " (only leading whitespace of original stripped after reverse) [E4]
    # - "\tlead" -> "dael\t" (tab is whitespace, moved to end, not stripped) [E6]
    # - " lead" -> "dael " (space preserved at end) [E6]
    # - "end\t " -> "dne" (original trailing "\t " stripped after reverse) [E8]
    # - "world  " -> "dlrow" [E11]
    # - "abc   " -> "cba" [E12]
    # - "   abc" -> "cba   " (leading spaces become trailing, preserved) [E12]
    # - "abc\u00a0" -> "cba" (non-breaking space is whitespace for strip) [E12]
    # - " \u00a0 abc" -> "cba \u00a0 " (leading whitespace of original stripped) [E12]
    # - "\u00a0" -> "" [E12]
    # - "abc\r\n" -> "cba" [E12]
    # So: reverse the string, then lstrip? No: reverse, then rstrip.
    # Wait: " lead" reversed = "dael ". Output "dael " keeps trailing space.
    # "trail " reversed = " liart". Output "liart" strips leading space.
    # So after reversing, we strip LEADING whitespace (lstrip).
    # Check "  x  " reversed = "  x  "; lstrip -> "x  ". Correct [E4].
    # "   abc" reversed = "cba   "; lstrip -> "cba   ". Correct [E12].
    # "abc\u00a0" reversed = "\u00a0cba"; lstrip -> "cba". Correct [E12].
    # " \u00a0 abc" reversed = "cba \u00a0 "; lstrip -> "cba \u00a0 ". Correct [E12].
    # "\u00a0" reversed = "\u00a0"; lstrip -> "". Correct [E12].
    # "\tlead" reversed = "dael\t"; lstrip -> "dael\t". Correct [E6].
    # "end\t " reversed = " \tdne"; lstrip -> "dne". Correct [E8].
    # "abc\r\n" reversed = "\n\rcba"; lstrip -> "cba". Correct [E12].
    # "a\tb " reversed = " b\ta"; lstrip -> "b\ta". Correct [E6].
    # "a \t b" reversed = "b \t a"; lstrip -> "b \t a". Correct [E8].
    # "abc\t" reversed = "\tcba"; lstrip -> "cba". Correct [E12].
    # "abc\n" reversed = "\ncba"; lstrip -> "cba". Correct [E12].
    # "abc  def   " reversed = "   fed  cba"; lstrip -> "fed  cba". Correct [E12].
    # So the rule is: output = s[::-1].lstrip()
    # (Python's str.lstrip with no args strips all whitespace including \u00a0,
    #  \t, \n, \r, \f, \v, and space.)
    inputs = probe.get("inputs", [])
    outputs = []
    for s in inputs:
        try:
            outputs.append(s[::-1].lstrip())
        except Exception:
            outputs.append("")
    return {"outputs": outputs}
